VERDICT: CLEAN

BOUNDARY: Edge cases are correctly handled. The requirement \(m \ge 1\) avoids the degenerate zero-dimensional space where some cited items (e.g., `lem-metrics-on-rn`) are not defined. The derivative is only defined at limit points of the domain, so isolated points are excluded. The integral is first defined for \(a<b\); the oriented extension covers \(a=b\) and \(a>b\) componentwise via `def-oriented-integral`, with no overlapping cases. The componentwise characterisation of differentiability and integrability relies on `thm-componentwise-limits-and-continuity`, which is valid for all \(m \ge 1\). The remark on norm independence correctly uses `thm-all-norms-on-rn-are-equivalent`; the derivative defined via \(\|\cdot\|_2\) is unchanged if another equivalent norm is used. No boundary counterexample was found.

SOURCES: Every load‑bearing cited item was inspected and matches the target’s usage. In particular: `def-vector-valued-functions-limits-and-continuity` (limit definition, uniqueness); `thm-componentwise-limits-and-continuity` (componentwise limit, used for derivative and integral); `def-derivative`, `def-darboux-integral`, `def-oriented-integral` (real analogues); `thm-linearity-of-the-integral`, `thm-algebra-of-derivatives` (componentwise algebra); `lem-integrability-on-a-subinterval`, `thm-additivity-over-subintervals` (splitting); `def-function-space`, `lem-standard-basis-of-f-n` (representation of \(\mathbb{R}^m\)). Non‑load‑bearing remarks also checked.

CHECKED: Title, public claim, every numbered (or bulleted) definitional step, the componentwise equivalence, the algebra of derivatives, the integral definition, linearity, restriction/splitting, oriented limits, and all Remarks were inspected. No mathematical inaccuracy, invalid inference, or mismatched citation was found.
